q: 1. The flow in a pipe or channel is said to be uniform when
options: the liquid particles at all sections have the same velocities
the liquid particles at different sections have different velocities
explain: Uniform flow is defined by velocity (and other flow parameters) remaining constant with respect to distance along the flow path.

q: 2. The flow in a pipe or channel is said to be non-uniform when
options: the liquid particles at all sections have the same velocities
the liquid particles at different sections have different velocities
the quantity of liquid flowing per second is constant
each liquid particle has a definite path
explain: Non-uniform flow occurs when the velocity changes from one cross-section to another at a given instant.

q: 3. According to equation of continuity
explain: For an incompressible fluid, the volume flow rate (Area * Velocity) must remain constant across different sections.

q: 4. A flow through a long pipe at constant rate is called
explain: Constant rate makes it steady; a long pipe of constant diameter makes it uniform.

q: 5. A flow through an expanding tube at constant rate is called
explain: It is steady (constant rate), but non-uniform because the expanding area causes velocity to change along the length.

q: 6. A flow whose streamline is represented by a curve, is called
explain: When flow velocity is a function of two space coordinates (e.g., x and y), the streamlines become curves in a plane.

q: 7. A flow whose streamline is represented by a straight line, is called _________ dimensional flow.
explain: In 1D flow, fluid parameters vary along a single direction, resulting in straight parallel streamlines.

q: 8. In one dimensional flow, the flow
explain: The key characteristic is that the flow parameters only change along the direction of flow, which is typically a straight line path.

q: 9. The total energy of a liquid particle in motion is equal to
options: pressure energy + kinetic energy + potential energy
explain: Based on Bernoulli's principle, total energy is the summation of these three forms of energy.

q: 10. The total head of a liquid particle in motion is equal to
options: pressure head + kinetic head + potential head
explain: Total head (H) = P/w + v²/2g + Z. It represents the energy per unit weight of the fluid.

q: 11. For a perfect incompressible liquid, flowing in a continuous stream, the total energy of a particle remains the same... This statement is called
explain: This is the core definition of Bernoulli's theorem for ideal fluid flow.

q: 12. According to Bernoulli's equation
explain: This represents the conservation of energy where potential, pressure, and kinetic heads sum to a constant value.

q: 13. Euler's equation in the differential form for the motion of liquids is given by
explain: Euler's equation relates pressure, gravity, and acceleration in a fluid, assuming no friction.

q: 14. Bernoulli's equation is applied to
explain: All three listed devices work by measuring pressure/velocity changes based on Bernoulli's principle.

q: 15. A pitot tube is used to measure the
options: velocity of flow at the required point in a pipe
pressure difference between two points in a pipe
total pressure of liquid flowing in a pipe
explain: The pitot tube measures stagnation pressure to determine the point velocity of the fluid.

q: 16. The hydraulic gradient line lies over the centre line of the pipe by an amount equal to the ............
explain: The Hydraulic Gradient Line (HGL) represents the sum of the datum head and pressure head ($P/w + z$).

q: 17. The total energy line lies over the centre line of the pipe by an amount equal to ............
explain: The Total Energy Line (TEL) represents the sum of pressure head, datum head, and velocity head ($P/w + z + v^2/2g$).

q: 18. When the flow in an open channel is gradually varied, the flow is said to be ............
explain: Gradually Varied Flow (GVF) is a type of steady non-uniform flow where the depth of flow changes gradually along the length of the channel.

q: 19. The flow of water through the hole in the bottom of a wash basin is an example of ............
explain: A free vortex occurs when liquid rotates without external torque, such as water draining from a basin or a whirlpool.

q: 20. The tangential velocity of the water element having a free vortex is ............
options: directly proportional to its distance from the centre
inversely proportional to its distance from the centre
directly proportional to its (distance)^2 from the centre
inversely proportional to its (distance)^2 from the centre
explain: In a free vortex, the velocity $v$ is inversely proportional to the radius $r$ ($vr = constant$).

q: 21. A flow in which ............ force is dominating over the viscosity is called turbulent flow.
explain: Turbulent flow is characterized by high inertia forces that overcome the damping effect of viscosity.

q: 22. The velocity at which the flow changes from laminar flow to turbulent flow is called ............
explain: The critical velocity is the threshold where the flow regime transitions between laminar and turbulent.

q: 23. Which of the following is an example of laminar flow?
options: Flow of oil in measuring instruments
explain: All these cases involve low velocities or high viscosities where the Reynolds number remains very low.

q: 24. The velocity at which the laminar flow stops, is known as ............
explain: The lower critical velocity is the speed below which any flow will eventually become laminar.

q: 25. Reynold's number is the ratio of the inertia force to the ............
explain: $Re = 	ext{Inertia Force} / 	ext{Viscous Force} = ho v D / \mu$.

q: 26. The velocity corresponding to Reynold number of 2000 is called ............
explain: The lower critical velocity in pipes typically corresponds to a Reynolds number of around 2000.

q: 27. The velocity corresponding to Reynold number of 2800, is called ............
explain: The upper or higher critical velocity corresponds to the Reynolds number where the flow becomes fully turbulent.

q: 28. The loss of pressure head in case of laminar flow is proportional to ...............
explain: According to the Hagen-Poiseuille equation for laminar flow, the pressure drop is directly proportional to the average velocity (v), unlike turbulent flow where it is proportional to v².

q: 29. In a footstep bearing, if the speed of the shaft is doubled, then the torque required to over-come the viscous resistance will be ...............
explain: In viscous lubrication, torque is proportional to the angular velocity (ω). If the speed doubles, the torque also doubles.

q: 30. In a footstep bearing, if the radius of the shaft is doubled, then the torque required to over-come the viscous resistance will be ...............
explain: Torque in a footstep bearing is proportional to the fourth power of the radius (R⁴). Thus, doubling the radius increases torque by 2⁴ = 16 times.

q: 31. When the Mach number is less than unity, the flow is called ...............
explain: Mach number (M) < 1 indicates the flow velocity is less than the local speed of sound, which is termed sub-sonic.

q: 32. When the mach number is between ............... the flow is called super-sonic flow.
explain: Supersonic flow occurs when 1 < Mach number < 6. Beyond M=6, the flow is typically classified as hypersonic.

q: 33. When the Mach number is more than 6, the flow is called ...............
explain: Flows with a Mach number greater than 5 or 6 are characterized by high temperature and dissociation effects, known as hyper-sonic flow.

q: 34. A flow is called sub-sonic, if the Mach number is ...............
explain: Sub-sonic flow is defined by a Mach number (M) less than 1 (unity).

q: 35. A flow is called super-sonic if the ...............
options: velocity of flow is very high
explain: Super-sonic flow is specifically defined by a Mach number greater than 1 but less than the hypersonic threshold (typically 6).

q: 36. A flow is called hyper-sonic, if the Mach number is ...............
explain: Since hyper-sonic flow requires a Mach number > 6, none of the specific ranges (M<1, M=1, or 1<M<6) apply.

q: 37. A point, in a compressible flow where the velocity of fluid is zero, is called ...............
explain: A stagnation point is a point in a flow field where the local velocity of the fluid is zero and all kinetic energy has been converted into pressure energy.

q: 38. The ratio of the inertia force to the viscous force is called ...............
explain: The Reynolds number (Re) is a dimensionless value used to predict flow patterns by comparing inertial forces to viscous forces.

q: 39. The ratio of the inertia force to the ............... is called Euler's number.
explain: Euler's number (Eu) is a dimensionless number representing the ratio between pressure forces and inertial forces.

q: 40. The ratio of the inertia force to the elastic force is called ...............
explain: The Mach number can also be defined as the square root of the ratio of inertia force to elastic force in a fluid.

q: 41. Froude's number is the ratio of inertia force to ...............
explain: Froude number (Fr) is a dimensionless number representing the ratio of inertial forces to gravitational forces. It is critical in open channel flow analysis.

q: 42. Reynold's number is the ratio of inertia force to ...............
explain: Reynolds number (Re) quantifies the relative importance of these two types of forces for given flow conditions, guiding whether a flow is laminar or turbulent.

q: 43. In fluids, steady, flow occurs when ...............
options: conditions of flow change steadily with time
conditions of flow do not change with time at a point
conditions of flow remain the same at adjacent point
velocity vector remains constant at a point
explain: Steady flow is defined as the type of flow in which the fluid properties (velocity, pressure, etc.) at any point do not change with time.

q: 44. A steady uniform flow is through ...............
options: a long pipe at decreasing rate
a long pipe at constant rate
an expanding tube at constant rate
an expanding tube at increasing rate
explain: Uniform flow requires a constant cross-section (long pipe), and steady flow requires a constant discharge (constant rate).

q: 45. A non-uniform steady flow is through ...............
options: a long tube at a decreasing rate
an expanding tube at constant rate
an expanding tube at increasing rate
a long pipe at increasing rate
explain: It is non-uniform because the cross-section changes (expanding tube) and steady because the discharge rate remains constant over time.

q: 46. The continuity equation ...............
options: expresses the relationship between work and energy
relates the momentum per unit volume between two points on a stream line
relates mass rate of flow along a stream line
requires that Newton's second law of motion be satisfied at every point in fluid
explain: The continuity equation is a mathematical expression of the law of conservation of mass for a fluid system.

q: 47. Equation of continuity of fluids is applicable only if ...............
options: flow is steady and velocity is uniform
explain: While general forms exist, the standard engineering version (A1V1 = A2V2) assumes steady, one-dimensional, and usually incompressible flow.

q: 48. For the two dimensional flow, the stream functions is given by Ψ = 2xy. The velocity at a point (3, 4) is ...............
explain: u = -∂Ψ/∂y = -2x = -6; v = ∂Ψ/∂x = 2y = 8. Resultant velocity V = √(u² + v²) = √((-6)² + 8²) = 10 m/sec.

q: 49. Euler's equation for the motion of liquids assumes that ...............
options: velocity of flow is non-uniform over the section
flow is unsteady along the stream line
explain: Euler's equation is derived for an ideal fluid, which is assumed to be non-viscous, homogeneous, and incompressible.

q: 50. For solving the problems is hydraulic engineering velocity used is ...............
options: velocity at the centre of pipe section
average velocity of flow over a section
mean of the velocities at the centre and that along the pipe surface
explain: Engineers use average (mean) velocity (V = Q/A) for practical calculations involving discharge and energy equations.
